Rashi on Temurah 14a:10:1.hebrew: הא איכא עולת העוף - תירוצא הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:10:1.english: But there is the bird burnt offering - This is [the Gemara's] answer.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:12:1.hebrew: אשם - הוי זכר, דכבש או איל כתיב ביה, ולא כבשה:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:12:1.english: A guilt offering - It is [only] a male, for "a lamb" or "a ram" is written regarding it, and not a ewe-lamb.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:12:2.hebrew: מאי ניהו שלמים - אבל שלמי צבור זכרים הם, דכתיב בהו (ויקרא כ״ג:י״ט) "ושני כבשים בני שנה לזבח שלמים". והם זבחי שלמי צבור, והם כבשי עצרת:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:12:2.english: What are they? Peace offerings - But the peace offerings of the community are males, as it is written regarding them (Leviticus 23:19): "And two lambs of the first year for a sacrifice of peace offerings." These are the communal peace offerings, [namely] the lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot].

Rashi on Temurah 14a:13:1.english: From where [do we derive] these matters - That communal offerings have no compensation [i.e., they are not brought at a later time if they were not offered at the proper time]:

Rashi on Temurah 14a:14:1.hebrew: דבר יום ביומו - במוספי המועדים משתעי בפרשת "שור או כשב", דכתיב "אלה מועדי ה' מקראי קדש וגו' להקריב אשה". ואיזה אשה מקריבין במועד יותר משאר ימים? הוי אומר: מוספין:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:14:1.english: Each day on its own day - It is speaking of the additional offerings of the festivals, in the passage of “an ox or a sheep” (Leviticus 22:27–23:44), as it is written: “These are the appointed seasons of the Lord, holy convocations, etc., to bring an offering made by fire.” And which offering made by fire do they bring on a festival more than on other days? You must say: the additional offerings.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:14:2.hebrew: שכל היום כשר למוספין - ובלבד שיקדמו מוספין לתמיד של בין הערבים, דאמר (ביומא דף לג.) "עליה השלם כל הקרבנות כולן":
Rashi on Temurah 14a:14:2.english: That the entire day is fit for the additional offerings - provided that the additional offerings precede the afternoon tamid offering, as it says (in Yoma 33a): “On it, complete all the offerings in their entirety.”

Rashi on Temurah 14a:15:1.hebrew: מנחתם ונסכיהם אפי' בלילה ואפי' למחר - אם קרב הקרבן בזמנו, ואפי' מכאן ועד עשרה ימים ולעולם, ובלא נזדמנו לו קא מיירי:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:15:1.english: “Their meal offerings and their libations” — even at night and even the next day - If the offering was sacrificed in its proper time, [the meal offerings and libations may be brought] even from now until ten days and forever; and [the baraita] is speaking of a case where [the meal offerings and libations] were not available to him.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:16:1.hebrew: מלבד שבתות ה' - דהכי כתי' בפסוק: זבח ונסכים דבר יום ביומו, מלבד שבתות ה'. ומשום דדרשינן סמוכים — דבר יום ביומו, הקרב נסכים — מלבד אותן של שבתות. דאם יו"ט אחר שבת הוא, הקרב נסכיו עם קרבנותיו, והקרב נסכים ששכחת אתמול ולא הקרבת:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:16:1.english: Beside the Shabbatot of the Lord - For so it is written in the verse: “a sacrifice and libations, each on its own day, beside the Shabbatot of the Lord.” And because we expound adjacent verses — “each on its own day” means: bring its libations — “beside” those of the Shabbatot, meaning: if the Festival falls after a Shabbat, one brings its libations together with its offerings, and also brings the libations that you forgot yesterday and did not bring.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:17:1.hebrew: ביום אין בלילה לא - דהא דבר יום ביומו כתיב, וסמיך ליה מלבד שבתות ה', כלומר, נסכי השבת תקריב היום ביו"ט, אבל בלילה לא:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:17:1.english: By day, yes; at night, no - For it is written "the matter of a day on its day," and immediately following it is "beside the Shabbatot of the Lord." That is to say, you may bring the libations of Shabbat today, on the Festival, but not at night.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:17:2.hebrew: ואי כתב מנחתם ונסכיהם הוה אמינא - שהיה בא ללמדך שתקריב נסכי היום בלילה הבא, אבל ביממא דלמחר לא:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:17:2.english: And if it had written "their meal offerings and their libations," I would have said - that it comes to teach you that you may bring the libations of the day during the night that follows, but not on the following day.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:18:1.hebrew: ומ"ש - כלומר, וכי תימא: מאי שנא דלימא בלילה אין, ביממא לא? הא קרא סתמא הוה כתיב:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:18:1.english: And what is different - That is, if you say: What is different, that [the verse] would say "at night, yes; by day, no"? [But] the verse was written without specification:

Rashi on Temurah 14a:18:2.hebrew: משום דבקדשים הלילה הולך אחר היום - שעבר, דכתיב (ויקרא ז) ביום קרבנו יאכל, לא תותירו ממנו עד בקר. אלמא כל הלילה קרי יום קרבנו. הלכך סד"א בלילה יקרב, דהנסכים הוי מיום שעבר, אבל ביממא דלמחר לא:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:18:2.english: Because with regard to sacrificial offerings, the night follows the day - that has passed. As it is written (Leviticus 7:15): "On the day of his offering it shall be eaten; you shall not leave any of it until morning." Evidently, the entire night is called "the day of his offering." Therefore, one might have thought [that the meal offering and libations] may be offered at night, since the libations are [obligations] from the day that has passed, but not during the day of the following morning.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:19:1.hebrew: אין לי כו' - בת"כ היא, ואקרא קאי, דכתיב: היא העולה על מוקדה על המזבח כל הלילה, שיהא נותנן מבוא השמש ומתעכלין כל הלילה:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:19:1.english: I have only, etc. - This is in the Torat Kohanim, and it refers to a verse, as it is written: "It is that which goes up on its firewood upon the altar all night" — that one must place them [on the altar] at sunset, and they are consumed all night.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:19:2.hebrew: אין לי אלא דברים שדרכן ליקרב בלילה כגון - אברים דעולה ופדרים, כדרבי להו לעיל, שיהא נותנן מבוא השמש, כלומר, לאחר שקיעת החמה נותנן על המערכה:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:19:2.english: I have only items that are normally sacrificed at night, for example - the limbs of the burnt offering and the fats, as [the Gemara] expanded upon them above, that one places them [on the altar] at sunset; that is to say, after the setting of the sun one places them on the altar.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:1:1.hebrew: קרבנות ציבור - כולם זכרים, דרובן עולות, ועולה זכר הוא. ואין ציבור מביאין שלמים, אלא כבשי עצרת, דזכרים הן. וחטאות שלהן שעירים, כדכתיב בכולהו "ושעיר חטאת אחד":
Rashi on Temurah 14a:1:1.english: Communal offerings - All of them are male, since most of them are burnt offerings, and a burnt offering is male. And the community does not bring peace offerings, except the lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot], which are male. And their sin offerings are goats, as it is written regarding all of them: "And one goat for a sin offering."

Rashi on Temurah 14a:20:1.hebrew: דברים שדרכן ליקרב ביום - דאינן קריבין בלילה כלל, דכולהו קרבנות כתיב בהו "ביום צוותו", דמשמע ביום ולא בלילה. אבל אברים ופדרים הוא דאיתרבו הכא בלילה מהאי קרא, שמקריבין מבוא השמש, וקא מקטירן על המערכה, והם מתעכלין מאיליהן. דאם לא כן, מהו שנאמר "היא העולה", מאי ממעט?:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:20:1.english: Items that are normally sacrificed in the day - That they are not offered at night at all, for with regard to all the offerings it is written "on the day He commanded them," which implies by day and not by night. But it is only limbs and fats that were included here, [to be offered] at night, from this verse: that one offers them at sunset and burns them on the arrangement of wood, and they are consumed on their own. For if not so, [what is the purpose of] the phrase "it is the burnt offering"? What does it exclude?

Rashi on Temurah 14a:20:2.hebrew: ופריך מבוא השמש - כלומר והאמרת דרכו ליקרב ביום:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:20:2.english: And [the Gemara] asks: "After sunset?" - But didn't you say that its manner is to be sacrificed during the day?

Rashi on Temurah 14a:21:1.hebrew: ליקדש - בלילה, אם ניתנו בכלי שרת, קדשי, דתו לא נפקי לחולין. אבל מיקרב, לא קרבי עד היום:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:21:1.english: For consecrating - At night, if they were placed in a service vessel, they become consecrated, and they no longer go out to non-sacred status. But as for being sacrificed, they are not sacrificed until the day.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:22:1.hebrew: אי מקדש קדשי - בלילה, מיקרב נמי קרבי:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:22:1.english: If it is consecrated, it is consecrated - at night, it should also be sacrificed [at night].

Rashi on Temurah 14a:22:2.hebrew: סמי מכאן נסכים - לא תימני להו עם דברים שדרכן ליקרב ביום:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:22:2.english: Delete from here [the item] libations - Do not count them among the things whose way is to be sacrificed in the day.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:23:1.hebrew: עם הזבח - שמביאין עם הזבח, וקידשן שחיטת הזבח, דהוי כי זבח גופיה, ואינן קריבין אלא ביום:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:23:1.english: With the offering - [Libations] that are brought with the animal offering, and the slaughter of the offering sanctified them, so that they are like the offering itself, and they may be sacrificed only by day.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:24:1.hebrew: אמר רב דימי אי אשכחיה אינשי כתיב איגרתא - אם הייתי מוצא אדם, הייתי כותב איגרתי, והייתי שולח אותה לרב יוסף לבבל:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:24:1.english: Rav Dimi said: If I find a person to write a letter - If I were to find a person, I would write my letter and send it to Rav Yosef in Babylonia.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:2:1.hebrew: קרבנות היחיד חייבין באחריותן - כלומר, יש מהן מאותן שקבוע להן זמן, שאפי' עבר זמנם חייבין להקריבן, כגון קרבן עולת יולדת (וקרבנה) וקרבנות מצורע: אם עבר שמיני שלו, יכול להקריבו לאחר זמן. אבל קרבנות ציבור שיש להן זמן, אם עבר זמנם בטל קרבנן, כדמפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Temurah 14a:2:1.english: Offerings of an individual are obligated in their compensation - That is to say, there are some of those [offerings] that have a fixed time, [and] even if their time has passed, one is obligated to bring them, such as the burnt offering of a woman who has given birth (and her offering) and the offerings of a leper: if his eighth day has passed, he can bring it after [its] time. But communal offerings that have a [fixed] time, if their time has passed, their offering is nullified, as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:4:1.hebrew: חביתי כהן גדול - דוחין שבת וטומאה, דכתיב בה "מנחה תמיד", "הרי היא לך כמנחת תמידין", בשילהי [התכלת] במנחות (דף נ:):
Rashi on Temurah 14a:4:1.english: The High Priest's griddle-cakes - They override Shabbat and ritual impurity, because it is written regarding it, "a continual meal-offering," [and the Gemara says], "Behold, it is for you like the meal-offering of the daily offerings," at the end of the chapter [entitled] HaTekhelet in Menachot (page 50b).

Rashi on Temurah 14a:4:2.english: The bull of Yom Kippur - The bull of Aaron [the High Priest]:

Rashi on Temurah 14a:4:3.hebrew: אלא שזמנו קבוע - כלומר, אין הטעם תלוי אלא בקביעות זמן. אותן שזמנן קבוע, שאם עבר הזמן אין להן תשלומין — דוחין שבת וטומאה, אפילו דיחיד. וכל שאין להן זמן קבוע — אינם דוחין שבת וטומאה, ואפי' דציבור, כגון פר העלם דבר של ציבור ושעירי עבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:4:3.english: Rather, [that] its time is fixed - That is to say, the reason depends only on the fixity of the time. Those whose time is fixed, such that if the time passes they have no make-up [offering] — they override Shabbat and impurity, even [offerings] of an individual. And any [offering] that has no fixed time does not override Shabbat and impurity, even [if it is one] of the community, such as the bull for an unwitting communal ruling [error] and the goats for idolatry.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:7:1.english: The primary offering - [This means] the first consecrated animal.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:8:1.hebrew: אפי' תימא רבנן - דלית להו ולד עושה תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:8:1.english: Even if you say [it is in accordance with] the Rabbis - who hold that the offspring [of an offering] does not render a substitute.

Rashi on Temurah 14a:9:1.hebrew: בין בזכרים בין בנקבות - משמע כל קרבן שחייב היחיד להביא, בין זכר בין נקבה:
Rashi on Temurah 14a:9:1.english: Both males and females - This implies that any offering that an individual is obligated to bring [may be] either male or female.

Tosafot on Temurah 14a:22:1.hebrew: וכל הקרב בלילה - פרש"י שילהי שתי הלחם (מנחות דף ק.): כגון שמן למנורה. ולא נראה, דמה קדושה שייכי ביה? הא לית ביה קדושת כלי. לכך נראה לומר דלא מצינו קרב בלילה אלא מנחת נסכים, ומשו"ה ניחא דלא משני הכא "דילמא אינו קדוש ליקדש, אבל קדוש ליפסל". דהכי מסיק התם שילהי פ' שתי הלחם (גז"ש) דסמיך אהא דתני "וכל הקרב בלילה", דלא מצינו קרב בלילה אלא מנחת נסכים בלבד. וה"ה דמצי למיפרך מינה הכא בהדיא, מדקתני "וכל הקרב בלילה" ולא מצינו דבר זה אלא מנחת נסכים בלבד; אלא דמהדר לפרוכי אף לפי מה דס"ד מעיקרא התם בפ' שתי הלחם:
Tosafot on Temurah 14a:22:1.english: "And any [offering] that is sacrificed at night" - Rashi explained, at the end of [the chapter] Shtei HaLechem (Menachot 100a): For example, the oil for the lamp. But this does not seem right, for what sanctity applies to it? It has no sanctity of a vessel. Therefore it seems to say that we do not find anything sacrificed at night except the meal offering accompanying libations, and for this reason it is understandable that [the Gemara] does not answer here, "Perhaps it cannot be consecrated, but it can become disqualified." For so it concludes there, at the end of the chapter Shtei HaLechem (gezerah shavah), which relies on this [baraita] that teaches "and any [offering] that is sacrificed at night," that we do not find anything sacrificed at night other than the meal offering accompanying libations alone. And similarly, [the Gemara] could have raised the objection from it here explicitly, since it teaches "and any [offering] that is sacrificed at night" and we find no such thing other than the meal offering accompanying libations alone; except that it goes back to object even according to what it initially supposed there, in the chapter Shtei HaLechem:
